metadata.title: TIMSS 2014/15 | Mathematics | Year 9: Trends over 20 years in TIMSS

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2014/15 lower secondary (Year 9) mathematics data for New Zealand, with sampling designed to represent the Year 9 school population. It applies TIMSS weighting to adjust means and proportions from the sample to the target population, explicitly noting that the overall sampling weight is a product of school, class, and student weights. The report also describes that standard errors reflect uncertainty from both sampling and the inference of proficiency from a subset of items. No replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is specified in the provided text, so replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed from this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report discusses TIMSS scaling and the use of item response theory to place achievement on a common scale, but it does not document a specific plausible-values (PV) strategy (e.g., Rubin’s rules) for the achievement estimates reported here. Because the excerpt does not provide an explicit missing-data handling method for the analytic sample, the missing-data approach cannot be verified. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, especially given that TIMSS analyses typically require documented handling of missing responses and PV-based scoring.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report analyzes New Zealand Year 9 students from TIMSS 2014/15, assessed in October–November 2014. Schools were sampled separately for Year 5 and Year 9 to minimize overlap, and at Year 9 level two classes were sampled with all Year 9 students in sampled classes included. New Zealand exclusions at the school level included very small schools (<4 Year 9 students), special education schools, the Correspondence School, and schools providing >50% instruction in te reo Māori; within-school exclusions included special education classes, special needs students, students with insufficient instruction in English, and units providing >50% instruction in te reo Māori. The report states the New Zealand exclusion rate for Year 9 was 3.1%.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2014/15 New Zealand report summarizes Year 9 mathematics achievement and its relationships with curriculum coverage, student background, and school/teacher context. It reports that New Zealand’s mean mathematics achievement in 2014/15 was statistically the same as 20 years earlier (1994/95) and not significantly different from 1998/99, 2002/03, and 2010/11, while being higher than 18 countries and lower than 17 (including other predominantly English-speaking countries). The report also finds that New Zealand’s strongest content area at Year 9 was data and chance (statistics), with greatest strength in reasoning and applying relative to knowing. Equity results show 6% of students reached the advanced benchmark and 15% were below the low benchmark, with a wider high–low range than in 2010/11. Methodologically, the report describes TIMSS scaling on a 500 (mean) / 100 (SD) scale, uses IRT-based proficiency inference, and applies TIMSS sampling weights, but it does not present machine-learning model performance metrics or document PV/missing-data procedures in the provided excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an official national TIMSS results report rather than an empirical machine-learning study. It provides descriptive and comparative statistics (means, benchmark proportions, significance tests) and contextual analyses, but it does not train or evaluate any ML predictive models, nor does it report ML-specific metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, and the extraction focuses on assessment design, sampling/weighting, and substantive TIMSS results.
